department: Department of Urban Forestry, Environment, and Natural Resources

deadline.value: Fall admission deadline is April 15, 2027 ($10 late fee thereafter; the 2024-2026 Catalog also lists May 1). Assistantship applications are due no later than two weeks after the admissions deadline.
deadline.quote: The Graduate School Admissions Application Deadlines SEMESTER/TERM APPLICATION FEE DEADLINE LATE FEE Fall $25.00 April 15 $10.00

also.quote: Admission Applications Deadlines Fall Semester May 1

Unless otherwise specified, applications for these awards should be made to the appropriate department chair or campus divisional office as early as possible, but no later than two weeks after the admissions application deadline for the applicable semester/term.

gre_subject.value: ETS does not offer a GRE Subject Test in Urban Forestry or Environmental Sciences.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Pre-admission supervisor commitment is not required; each graduate student is assigned/selects an advisor at the time of admission in consultation with the department chair and graduate coordinator.
supervisor.quote: Every graduate student must be assigned an advisor in his/her academic department. At the time of admission, the student, in consultation with the department chairperson and the graduate coordinator, will select an advisor

funding.value: Assistantship, scholarship, and internship opportunities are available through the department and Graduate School, awarded competitively and contingent on availability of funds (assistantship/fellowship recipients are usually exempted from out-of-state fees for up to 4 years).
funding.quote: Many assistantship and scholarship and internship opportunities exist for students pursuing urban forestry degrees.

also.quote: Contingent on availability of funds, all graduate assistantships/fellowship are awarded on a semester basis ... The maximum time limit (academic year and summer) for doctoral assistantships and fellowships is four (4) academic years.

entry_route.value: A master's degree in urban forestry, forestry, natural resources, plant/soil sciences, biology, chemistry, environmental sciences, or a related area is required for all applicants (with remedial coursework if entering from another discipline).
entry_route.quote: A master's degree in urban forestry, forestry, renewable and natural resources, plant and soil sciences, biology, chemistry, natural and environmental sciences, and other related areas are required for all applicants.

notes: Concentrations in Urban Forest Science and Urban Forest Management. Requires minimum 3.0 graduate GPA, GRE scores, research/career goals essay, and 3 recommendation letters (2 from major-field advisors).
name: Ph.D. in Urban Forestry
